name: Grounding DINO and MM-Grounding-DINO (open-vocabulary, Swin-T and Swin-B)
plain: IDEA Research's Grounding DINO and OpenMMLab's MM-Grounding-DINO (tiny, base; Swin backbone, BERT text encoder): open-vocabulary detector, finds boxes for class names given as text at call time (default: the 80 COCO classes). Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: Grounding DINO (Liu et al. 2023, IDEA Research): open-set detection that fuses a Swin image backbone with a BERT text encoder in a DINO-style deformable transformer; each of 900 queries scores every caption token. MM-Grounding-DINO (Zhao et al. 2024, OpenMMLab) is the same network with a scaled, biased contrastive class head and unshared decoder heads, retrained on Objects365, GoldG and V3Det. Pass `text=[...]` at call time (default: the 80 COCO class names), joined into one caption; a class score is the mean token score of its name. Images are resized to 800 px on the short side (at most 1333 on the long side). The portable `module()` is the image side with the COCO caption's text features as constants.

papers.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
An Open and Comprehensive Pipeline for Unified Object Grounding and Detection

official.reason: fastforks follows the Hugging Face transformers port, which loads the IDEA-Research/grounding-dino-* weights, instead of the authors' repository.
The MM-Grounding-DINO authors' code lives in MMDetection; fastforks follows the Hugging Face transformers port that loads the converted weights.

limitations: Requires the optional transformers library (the network is its `GroundingDinoForObjectDetection`).

The original in the benchmarks and goldens is the Hugging Face transformers 5.19.0 port with the authors' weights (IDEA-Research/grounding-dino-*, openmmlab-community/mm_grounding_dino_*); the official GroundingDINO and mmdetection code (their CUDA deformable-attention ops) was not run.
Class names are joined into one caption of at most 256 tokens (about 100 short names); a longer list raises an error instead of being split into several passes.
No phrase output: `labels` index into the given names (the token-level text threshold of the Hugging Face post-processing is not used).
grounding-dino-base was trained with COCO (and RefCOCO, ODinW) data: its COCO numbers are not zero-shot.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: boxes, class labels, scores and instance masks.
